# NOTES: "The Templeton Case" by Victor L. Whitechurch (Gutenberg #75669; pub. Edward J. Clode, Inc., NY; 1924 text)

Single book, no BOOK headings. 21 chapters.

## Cast
- **Tom Gale**: crew/cook of little schooner *Lucy*, moored at Marsh Quay; gossip; smokes pipe; later gives cigar to... (received cigar from Grayson; Colson gives him 2 cigars).
- **Reginald Templeton**: victim, ~50s, Fellow of Royal Geographical Society, explorer, returned from Africa/South Africa, bachelor, reticent, owns yacht *Firefly* (white, green line, cutter-rigged, auxiliary oil engine). Stabbed in back, dagger-like triangular wound.
- **Jim Webb**: crew of *Firefly*, from 31 Fore Street, Salcombe; works for Mr. Jefferies (boat hirer); uncle at Frattenbury. Found body Sunday morning.
- **Mrs. Yates**: widow, landlady of "Mariner's Arms" (rosy, stout); toothache night of murder; late husband's walking-stick (brown, knob).
- **Harold Grayson**: artist lodger at Mariner's Arms (~25, fair curly hair, clear blue eyes, cigars, shell-shock WWI; father Osmond Grayson, county magistrate, home near Marlow, Bucks). Fiancé of Winnie Cotterill later. Left Sunday morning on bicycle. Detained at Linderton (cottage of Mrs. Goring; Constable Drake). Released.
- **Mr. Proctor** (Joseph): bald, egg-shaped head, clean-shaven, velveteen jacket, woollen slippers; retired cigar merchant (two years at Marsh Quay; formerly in cigar trade; Swiss photo of Julier Pass; Engadine). Foreman of jury. Lives opposite inn. Great-nephew **Philip ("Phil")**, ~15, bicycle, eel-spearing. Cook-housekeeper and young maid. Stays at Merrifield's: alibi via bridge with **Stephen Merrifield** (corn merchant, Frattenbury), left at 1:30 am. Owns cigar cupboard with boxes of Canon's brand. Arrested then released.
- **Isaac Moss**: small dark Jewish diamond dealer, 13a Hatton Garden; villa "Fairview," 53 Compton Avenue, Brondesbury; villa at Marsh Quay opposite (caretakers: Mr. and Mrs. ... ; wife ~35). Agent for Ehbrenstein & Co. (South Africa); 32 uncut diamonds, 31 found, one missing. Visited yacht ~1 am Sunday in boat, found body, panicked; stone was in Templeton's waistcoat pocket. Alibi: Hotel "Chester," room 87, porter saw him till after midnight. Wife present at inquest.
- **Canon Charles Fittleworth**: cathedral canon, Frattenbury Close; cousin of Templeton; ~40–50, pince-nez, keen brown eyes. Wife Mrs. Fittleworth; daughter **Doris**; maid **Jane**. Has box of cigars from Spanish friend **De Garcia** (Cuba, planters' brand). Found red-and-gold cigar band on yacht cabin floor; hid it, produced at inquest; coroner rebuked him. Dined with Templeton Saturday (Templeton left ~8:30 pm, had "call" in Frattenbury). Brother retired colonel attended funeral.
- **Francis Norwood**: solicitor and coroner, Georgian street, brass plate; hatchet face, mutton-chop whiskers, never married; stiff; left-handed (drew cork with left hand; carried stick in left hand). Former clerk Ezra Grice; partner-era embezzlement by Norwood, blamed on Percy Forbes. Speculating heavily in "Virginian Reefs." Hanged himself in cell with braces (night after arrest). Murderer.
- **Superintendent Thomas Norton**: quiet, refined, big black moustache; sympathetic. Chief Constable **Major Renshaw**, military, close-cropped moustache, lives outside city, dresses for dinner.
- **Detective-Sergeant Bob Colson**: slight, clean-shaven, alert, shrewd grey eyes; careful slow thinker; wife (unnamed, "pleasant little wife"; intuition, helps). Lives outside city walls. Carries small automatic pistol. Uses red glass to signal. Cycled. Uses "diplomatic cigar case."
- **Constable Gadsden**: burly, pocket-book; relieved by Peters. Constable Peters.
- **Constable Thompson**, **Tyler** (plainclothes, shadowed Moss).
- **Mr. Blake**: tobacconist (sold matching walking-stick; ferrule Swiss).
- **Dr. Hazell**: small, round-faced, gossip, bought 500 "Virginian Reefs."
- **Sir Peter Birchnall**: baronet, magistrate, recommended Virginian Reefs.
- **Rev. Alfred Carringford**: vicar.
- **Anthony Crosby**: London lawyer, Crosby & Paxton, 17b Lincoln's Inn Fields; tall, clean-shaven; stayed at "Dolphin" hotel; executor; advertised; reward £50.
- **Winifred "Winnie" Cotterill** (real name Forbes): ~25, art illustrator, grey eyes, flat with Maude Wingrave (Battersea Park, high block); sub-editress Maude. Inherits ~£2,000. Engaged to Grayson.
- **Ezra Grice**: ex-clerk of Norwood; ~44 now; South Africa; joined Templeton; arm broken, fever; saved by Zulu medicine man; later "dead" rumour; arrived Plymouth December 8 (wire from Sir James).
- **Sir James Perrivale**: tall, weather-beaten, big-game hunter; camp beyond Umbrati river; Colonel Ottery witness.
- **Percy Forbes**: Winnie's father, lawyer; embezzlement, 7 years penal servitude, died Princetown.
- **Mabel Cotterill**: Winnie's mother (Mrs. Forbes); Templeton was in love with her.
- **Peter's Magazine**, **The Holborn** (editors), **Mr. Buckland** (chemist, walrus moustache, remembers Grice).
- **George Simmonds**: cottager who met Templeton on path, 5:30–6 pm Saturday.
- **Joe Thatcher**: poacher, midnight; saw Moss rowing across ~12:30–1 am, bumping yacht; saw car at ~1 am (Merrifield's).
- **Dean**: got cigars from Canon (dozen; smoked, took box).
- **Tom Gale's cigar** from Grayson.

## Places
- **Marsh Quay**: quay on eastern shore of estuary off Channel, 2 miles south of Frattenbury Cathedral (grey tapering spire). Quay ~50 yds; anchorage pool; "Mariner's Arms" (inn, parlour with five ship models, Nelson oleographs); across estuary: wood, stony patch, landing-stage, Moss's villa. Estuary mud at low tide; strong tide.
- **Frattenbury**: cathedral city; the Close; South Street; Cross; Canal Basin; police station at bottom of South Street; Dolphin hotel; Deanery; Norwood's office/house; Town Hall; cemetery; Magistrates' Court; "Blue Lion"/Selham "Wheatsheaf" (Grayson's alibi).
- **Linderton**: village 4–5 miles north; Grayson detained there.
- **Hatton Garden** (Moss office); **Lincoln's Inn Fields**; **British Museum** newspaper room; **Scotland Yard**.
- **Salcombe**, **Plymouth**, **Ryde** (G.P.O.), **Poole**, **Weymouth**, **Dartmouth**, **Langham**, **Selham** (3 miles down estuary), **Princetown**, **Cape Town**, **Johannesburg**, **Umbrati river**.

## Timeline (Sat 1 Oct? Oct Saturday–Monday approx.)
1. **Saturday, early afternoon (~1 pm)**: Templeton arrives *Firefly* at Marsh Quay; Tom Gale chats; Grayson present (Templeton "from Africa, Mr. Reginald Templeton"; Grayson asks name). Templeton gives Grayson cigar band; Grayson gives Tom cigar.
2. Templeton crosses estuary to Moss's house (~afternoon); Grayson sees; Moss shows him Moss's house (Moss rowing). Diamonds: Templeton gives bag, receives receipt; keeps bag; 32 stones delivered; Moss took 31 home (one in bag).
3. Templeton walks to Frattenbury, dines with Canon Fittleworth (arrives 5–6, dinner 7, leaves ~8:30; "call" in Frattenbury). Postman saw him leaving Close ~8:30–9.
4. Templeton walks back by stile field path; ~10 pm dark. Pirate Colson's walking-stick ferrule trail: Templeton carried stick in right hand (inbound).
5. Templeton's appointment with Norwood (typed letter: "call next Saturday evening after 8.30—not later than 9").
6. Night (~11 pm–1 am): Norwood on yacht; killed Templeton; took pocketbook; Moss rowed over ~12:30–1 am, found body, fled. Walking-stick (Norwood's) left in dinghy under stern seat.
7. **Sunday ~6:30–7:30 am**: Jim Webb discovers body; Mrs. Yates; Proctor; Phil rides to Frattenbury; Superintendent Norton; Dr. (unnamed); Colson left aboard; Canon finds cigar band Sunday; Grayson leaves early Sunday.
8. Sunday: Mr. Moss and wife leave by 7:35 train; Colson's inquiries; Colson rides back Saturday after dark; overnight watch (Sunday night: canoe-thief = Proctor).
9. Monday: Colson recovers canoe; Proctor retrieves; Phil found canoe; Colson tests Proctor.
10. Tuesday: Inquest adjourned; Grayson detained; Canon identifies cigar band swap; burial Tuesday afternoon.
11. Wednesday–Thursday: Moss interview (Hatton Garden); Crosby; Proctor interview; Thatcher statement.
12. Later: Ezra Grice identified; Sir James Perrivale; Norwood arrested at Canon's dinner.

Notes for other chapter details: Chapter IX Colson's notes; Chapter XVI Proctor's confession: Merrifield alibi, cigar band changed by jurymen? (Later: Colson says juror Bailey or Westall changed band; actually Norwood changed it, picking up band from grate). Final: Norwood arrested Chapter XX; suicide in cell Chapter XXI; Ezra Grice statement; Crosby to consider telling Winnie about her father.

## Key objects
- Red-and-gold cigar band (Canon's Cuban brand; swapped by Norwood at inquest with Grayson's band from grate).
- Chamois bag with diamond (one "size of a pea," Moss's).
- Blotting-pad: "Ezra Grice's confession & proof. This is final." (typed "Ezra's ices").
- Walking-stick: plain ash, crook handle, Alpine square ferrule, small chip on handle (Norwood's; dummy stick planted by Colson).
- Canoe (Proctor's; cleat boards). Dinghy (green paint smear on bows).
- Typewritten letter: "I shall be at home to discuss matters if you will call next Saturday evening after 8.30—not later than 9."
- Notes/banknote £100 from Templeton's letter; Templeton will: £2,000 to Winnie.
- Letter from A. F. Crosby.
- Virginian Reefs stock (Norwood & Hazell lost money).

## Final
Norwood: suicide with braces (overnight). Canon: "I want time to think it over." Crosby undecided about telling Winnie of father's conviction (Percy Forbes).
